title: Garbage Island
novel: Marshall became [[obsessed|obsess]] with saving the environment after watching a [[documentary|documentary]] about a giant island of garbage floating in the Pacific Ocean. The images of [[polluted|pollute]] waters and suffering sea animals [[haunted|haunt]] him day and night. He started bringing reusable bags everywhere, [[composting|compost]] his food waste, and giving his friends long [[lectures|lecture]] about recycling. Lily was [[supportive|supportive]] but also worried that Marshall was going too far. Meanwhile, Ted ran into Zoey's ex-husband, The Captain, at an art gallery. The Captain was surprisingly [[cordial|cordial]] and invited Ted to look at his [[paintings|painting]]. Ted was nervous because he was now dating Zoey, and The Captain did not seem to know about their relationship. The Captain talked about his life since the [[divorce|divorce]] and mentioned that he had moved on. Ted felt a wave of [[relief|relief]], but also a strange sense of [[guilt|guilt]]. On the other side of town, Barney admitted his feelings for Nora. He told the gang that he had been thinking about her [[constantly|constant]] and that he wanted to ask her out properly. Robin was visibly [[hurt|hurt]] by this news, though she tried to hide it. She had been developing feelings for Barney again without realizing it. Marshall's environmental obsession reached a [[peak|peak]] when he tried to swim to the garbage island to clean it up himself. Lily stopped him at the last minute and told him that he could make a bigger [[difference|difference]] by working within the system rather than doing something [[reckless|reckless]]. Marshall agreed and decided to look for a job at an environmental [[organization|organization]]. Barney took Nora on a proper date and was genuinely [[nervous|nervous]] for the first time in years. The episode ended with the gang reflecting on how far they had all come and how much they still had to learn about love, [[responsibility|responsibility]], and the planet they shared.

documentary.en: a film or program about real events

pollute.en: to make air, water, or land dirty

haunt.en: to keep coming back to someone's mind

compost.en: to recycle food waste into soil

lecture.en: a long talk given to teach or scold

supportive.en: giving help and encouragement to someone

painting.en: a picture made with paint on a surface

divorce.en: the legal end of a marriage

relief.en: a feeling of comfort after worry ends

guilt.en: a bad feeling about something you did wrong

hurt.en: to cause emotional or physical pain

difference.en: a change that has a noticeable effect

reckless.en: doing things without thinking of danger

organization.en: a group formed for a shared purpose

responsibility.en: a duty to deal with something or someone
